rootCauseHypothesis:
The hosted service appears to enforce a desktop-only authorization mechanism for workspace pairing, so the browser-based test cannot complete sign-in. The Connect workspace button is trying to open a WrazyOS desktop authorization URL that is blocked in this environment, which suggests the backend or frontend is returning an auth link/intent that only works on the native desktop client instead of a web-capable authorization flow. Underlying error: TEST BLOCKED

The workspace pairing could not be completed — the sign-in flow requires the WrazyOS desktop authorization URL which cannot be opened in this browser-based test environment.

Observations:
- Clicking 'Connect workspace' produced a persistent notification: 'Sign-in could not open — Only the WrazyOS desktop authorization URL can be opened.'
- The Server settings field is already set to 'https://srv1726015.tailbf7608.ts.net' and the page confirmed 'Settings saved', so server configuration is correct but pairing is blocked by desktop-only authorization.

recommendedFixTarget.rationale: Make the workspace pairing/sign-in flow browser-compatible or provide a web fallback for authorization. Specifically, avoid hard-requiring the WrazyOS desktop authorization URL in the Connect workspace action; instead support opening an HTTPS/OAuth-style consent page in the browser, or return a pairing code/redirect flow that can complete without a desktop app. If desktop-only auth is intentional, update the hosted environment to expose the correct desktop authorization endpoint and ensure the app can deep-link/launch it from the browser context, but the practical fix is to add a web-based auth endpoint and route the service to use it when running outside WrazyOS desktop.
